What AI agent permissions are.

Rules for what an AI agent may do with your customer's login. Each action gets one of four answers.

Allow

The request goes through as usual.

Mask

The page loads, private fields come back empty. The agent can still help.

Ask owner

The request waits until the account owner approves it with a passkey. An agent cannot approve itself.

Block

The agent is refused. A person takes the session back with a passkey.

One rule, four situations.

The same customer can be at the keyboard one minute and hand over to an agent the next. So each rule answers per situation.

AI agent

Agent tool traces in the page, a signed agent request, or clicks no hand could make.

AI browser

The page is open in an AI app's browser, but nothing shows an agent acting yet. The person's first real click unlocks it.

Not sure

Too little signal. Never treated as a person.

Person

Human clicks or a passkey. Always allowed.

Questions

Something missing? Write to arif@onehuman.ai.

What are AI agent permissions?

Rules for what an AI agent may see and do when it acts with a customer's login in your app. Each action gets one answer per situation: allow, mask, ask the owner, or block.

Is this for AI agents my company builds?

No. It is for the agents your customers bring into your app with their own login. For agents you build, give each one its own identity and scopes in your authorization system.

How is this different from OAuth scopes?

Scopes cover apps a customer connects to your API. A browser agent never asks for a scope: it uses the customer's own browser, cookies and login. So the rules have to work inside the session, per request. How OneHuman does it →

Which AI agents do the rules cover?

Claude in Chrome, Claude desktop, ChatGPT agent, OpenAI Codex, Perplexity Comet, Playwright and Puppeteer. What each one does against a protected page →

Will my real customers notice?

Rarely. A person is always allowed, and their clicks are checked as they happen. In our tests 2 of 397 human clicks were read as a program. Start with watch first to see every decision before anything is enforced. How we measured →

What does "ask owner" mean?

The request is held. The account owner approves it with a passkey (Touch ID, Windows Hello), and the approval covers only that request: same action, same amount, same recipient.

Can I use the rules without OneHuman?

Yes. The plain-English rules work as a spec for any stack or a security review. The JSON file is OneHuman's policy format, and npx onehumanai init puts it to work on a Node.js server. Read the docs →

Is anything I pick here sent to you?

No. The generator runs in your browser. The share link keeps your choices after the #, which never reaches a server.

What does it cost to run the rules?

Nothing up to 100 customers a month whose AI agents use your app. You pay only for those customers. Pricing →
